Title: Redis-backed caching for slow backend reads, starting with Friends overview
Category: backend
Priority: P1

get-spec output:
Switching from Profile to Friends (and likely other reads) is slow every time -- there is currently zero caching on backend read endpoints. friends_overview (backend/users/friends.py) runs three uncached DB queries on every call. The infrastructure for Redis already exists and is unused for this: backend/backend/settings.py wires Django CACHES with a three-tier fallback (Redis via REDIS_URL, else shared DatabaseCache, else local LocMemCache), redis is already in requirements.txt, and backend/users/leaderboard.py has its own separate direct-redis-client pattern for sorted-set ranking only. Task: 1) Research and pick the best-fit managed Redis provider for this stack (Vercel serverless Django + Supabase Postgres already using a transaction pooler due to IPv6/connection issues, see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) -- weigh HTTP/REST-based options that avoid persistent-connection problems in serverless, not just the cheapest choice. Document exact setup steps (account, env var names, region) in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md but do NOT create the account or spend money -- the owner adds real credentials afterward. 2) Using the existing Django CACHES abstraction (not the leaderboard raw-client pattern), add caching to friends_overview and audit other slow, frequently-repeated reads across trivia/ and users/ for the same treatment, with correct invalidation (e.g. friends_overview must invalidate immediately on a friend/request/block action for the affected users, not just time out). 3) Must work correctly with zero Redis configured today (falls back to DatabaseCache). This is an infrastructure-level, multi-endpoint change -- treat as needing a real design pass, not a single-file patch.

# Friends & Leaderboard — Caching and Scaling Plan

A plan, not a to-do list for right now. Nothing here should be built until a
real number (see "When to actually do this") says it's worth it. Written
2026-09-19 alongside the friends-search feature, to record the reasoning
before it's forgotten.

## Where things stand today

| Data | Backed by | Cached? |
|---|---|---|
| Global leaderboard (top 100, rank, total) | `users/leaderboard.py` | **Yes** — Redis ZSET (`leaderboard`, member = public_id, score = points) when `REDIS_URL` is set; falls back to plain Postgres queries otherwise. Already scales to any N via `ZREVRANGE`/`ZREVRANK` (O(log N)). |
| Friends leaderboard (`?scope=friends`) | `leaderboard.friends_board()` | No — always Postgres, deliberately (see below). |
| Friend list / friend search (`search-friends`) | `users/friends.py` | No — always Postgres. |
| Friend requests, blocked list (`friends-overview`) | `users/friends.py` | No — always Postgres. |

The global leaderboard cache exists because **N (total players) is
unbounded** and a top-100/rank query over the whole table gets slower as the
platform grows — a classic case where a sorted-set cache pays for itself.

## Why friends data isn't a scaling problem the same way

Every friends query is bounded by **your own friend count**, not by the
total user base:

- `search-friends` resolves "which users are my friends" via two indexed
  lookups on `Friendship.user_low`/`user_high` (bounded by your friend
  count), *then* filters/paginates that already-small set. It never scans
  the whole `CustomUser` table.
- `friends_board()` does the same thing before sorting by points.
- `friends-overview`'s requests/blocked lists are similarly bounded by
  "requests you're personally involved in."

No realistic friend count (even a very socially active account) approaches
the row counts where an indexed Postgres query over that person's own rows
becomes slow. This is different in kind from the global leaderboard, where
N is "everyone who has ever signed up." **Caching this today would add
invalidation complexity for a problem that doesn't exist yet.**

## Where Redis would actually help, if/when it's needed

I've classified this as **hard, high-risk and needing a design round**. Opus implements from a plan that Fable writes.

- **Why it's hard:** it's infrastructure-wide and touches several endpoints. Every friend, request and block action needs cache invalidation for the affected users, and an audit across `trivia/` and `users/` has to decide which reads get cached. The provider research and the setup steps for `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` are a separate thread. The spec also asks for a real design pass.
- **Why it's high risk:** it touches the `CACHES` layer in `backend/backend/settings.py`, plus friends and blocking in `backend/users/`. The classify rubric lists all of these as high-risk surfaces.
- **Why Opus:** high risk sends it to Opus, and so does being a hard task with a plan.
- **Money:** the spec already says not to create the Redis account or spend anything. The design round should keep provider work to research and docs, and leave credentials to you.
- **Conflict for the design round:** `docs/CACHING_SCALING_PLAN.md` (written 2026-09-19) argues against caching friends data yet, because the invalidation work isn't worth it at current sizes. This card overrides that on purpose, so the round should update that doc rather than follow it.
- **Mislabelled rule:** the risk-high list the rubric points to as AUTH-11 isn't there. AUTH-11 in `AUTH_CONSTRAINTS.md` covers token-refresh waiters. The rubric's own text was enough to set high risk here.

I didn't treat any pick as a close call, so I added nothing to `DECISIONS.md`.
